payload.text:
**Don't merge yet. `canEdit` has a bug that lets view-only users edit documents.** All the tests pass, but they don't catch it. I didn't change any code.

**1. `canEdit` checks the wrong right (src/guard.js)**
```js
return share.mask & WRITE === WRITE && !share.locked;
```
In JavaScript, `===` is evaluated before `&`, so this runs as `share.mask & (WRITE === WRITE)`, which is `mask & true`, which is `mask & 1`. That checks READ, not WRITE. I ran it to confirm:
- A view-only share (`mask: READ`, unlocked) returns **true**, so viewers can edit.
- A share with COMMENT and WRITE but no READ returns **0**, so it's refused.

The tests miss it because the only editor in them has READ as well as WRITE. The fix is to use `hasRight(share.mask, WRITE)`, like `canComment` does. It's also worth adding a test that a view-only share can't edit.

**2. `transferOwnership` doesn't validate its inputs (src/ownership.js)**
- If `fromUser` has no share, `undefined &= ~ADMIN` quietly creates a share for them with no rights (`0`).
- If `fromUser` isn't actually the current owner, it still removes their ADMIN and hands ownership to `toUser`. Checking `doc.owner === fromUser` (or that the caller has ADMIN) would make this safer, unless the calling code already does that check.

**3. Smaller points**
- `toggleRight` does what the README says. But the dialog can switch READ off while WRITE stays on, which leaves an editor who can't view the document. It can also remove the owner's own ADMIN. Decide whether the dialog should prevent those.
- There's no test that a switch turns a right **off**. The README describes both directions, but only turning a right on is tested.
- Missing tests: view-only share can't edit (this would have caught #1), and ownership transfer when `fromUser` has no share.
- The changelog only mentions editors and locking. It leaves out the share-dialog switches and ownership transfer that this release also adds.

Everything else looks fine: `canComment`, the locking rules, and the version bump.
